title: 3rd Truth The Importance Of This Mystery And Reference To The Risale I Nur

questions.question: What is this passage mainly trying to explain?
questions.answer: It is explaining a deep proof of Allah’s oneness and how Allah can create great and small things with the same ease.

questions.question: How does the passage describe this truth in Islam and faith?
questions.answer: It describes it as a very important foundation for Islam and a deep source of faith.

questions.question: What effect does understanding this truth have on the Qur’an’s message?
questions.answer: It helps open its deep meanings and helps people understand a hidden secret about creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to philosophy when facing this mystery?
questions.answer: It says philosophy becomes unable to solve it.

questions.question: Who is thanked and praised in the passage?
questions.answer: The Compassionate Creator, Allah, is thanked and praised.

questions.question: What work is said to have explained and proven this difficult matter?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is said to have explained and proven it.

questions.question: How certain does the passage say these proofs are?
questions.answer: It says they are as certain as a simple math fact that cannot be denied.

questions.question: Does the passage give the full explanation here, or does it point readers to other parts for the full discussion?
questions.answer: It points readers to other parts for the full discussion and only plans a short outline here.

questions.question: What does the passage say the writer wanted to present briefly?
questions.answer: The writer wanted to present the basic supports and proofs of this mystery.

questions.question: How many mysteries does the writer say would be mentioned like steps or a table of contents?
questions.answer: Thirteen.

questions.question: How much of those mysteries had already been written?
questions.answer: The first two had already been written.

questions.question: Why did the writer stop before finishing the rest?
questions.answer: Two strong obstacles, one physical and one non-physical, caused him to stop.

questions.question: What special idea about Allah’s creation is at the center of this passage?
questions.answer: The idea is that the biggest and smallest created things are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: Why is this idea described as a mystery or riddle?
questions.answer: Because it is very deep, hard for the mind to fully reach on its own, and needs clear explanation.

questions.question: What does the passage say this truth helps uncover about all created things?
questions.answer: It helps uncover a hidden secret in how all beings are created.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the value of this truth for a Muslim’s belief?
questions.answer: It teaches that this truth is one of the greatest supports of belief in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What feeling does the writer show after saying this truth was explained?
questions.answer: The writer shows strong gratitude and praise to Allah.

questions.question: What book or collection is named as the place where this mystery was solved and proved?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What kind of proofs does the passage say were used there?
questions.answer: Strong and decisive proofs.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention different sections of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: To show where readers can find fuller explanations of this matter.

questions.question: Instead of repeating the whole proof here, what does the writer choose to do?
questions.answer: He chooses to give only a short summary of the foundations and proofs.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to describe the thirteen mysteries?
questions.answer: It compares them to thirteen steps or a contents list.

questions.question: According to the passage, what truth of faith is being clarified?
questions.answer: The truth that Allah’s oneness is shown in His power to create all things, whether huge or tiny, with no difference in difficulty.

questions.question: How is this truth connected to the “word of unity”?
questions.answer: It is presented as part of the meaning and proof of declaring Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage call this truth besides a proof?
questions.answer: It calls it a useful wisdom, a great key, and a deep mystery.

questions.question: What does understanding this mystery allow people to know better?
questions.answer: It allows people to better know a hidden secret about how creation works.

questions.question: What limit of human thinking is pointed out in the passage?
questions.answer: It points out that philosophy cannot solve this mystery by itself.

questions.question: What response does the writer have after saying the mystery was solved?
questions.answer: The writer responds with much praise and thanks to Allah.

questions.question: What is said about the certainty of the proof in the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Its certainty is described as completely clear and firm.

questions.question: Does the passage claim to prove the matter only in one place or in several parts of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It says the matter was proven in several parts.

questions.question: What does the writer say he will do in this passage instead of giving every detail?
questions.answer: He says he will briefly mention the main bases and proofs.

questions.question: How many mystery-topics does he intend to point to?
questions.answer: Thirteen.

questions.question: What had already been completed from that list?
questions.answer: The first and second mystery had been written.

questions.question: What comparison in the passage shows Allah’s unlimited power in creation?
questions.answer: It says that for Allah, the largest universal thing and the smallest individual thing are the same in ease.

questions.question: Why is this truth called one of the greatest bases of Divine unity?
questions.answer: Because it strongly shows that only Allah has such complete power over all creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say this explanation does to the hidden meanings of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It opens them up like a key opening something closed.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the hidden matter about creation that is being explained?
questions.answer: It describes it as a very secret and hard-to-know puzzle.

questions.question: Which human way of thinking is said to be powerless before this puzzle?
questions.answer: Philosophy is said to be powerless before it.

questions.question: What attitude does the writer show toward Allah after mentioning this solution?
questions.answer: He shows deep thankfulness and praise.

questions.question: What is the name of the work that the writer says solved this puzzle?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How strong does the writer say the proofs are in that work?
questions.answer: He says they are firm, clear, and beyond serious doubt.

questions.question: Why are readers directed to other sections of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Because those sections give the fuller explanation of this subject.

questions.question: What smaller goal does the writer keep for this passage?
questions.answer: He keeps the smaller goal of briefly laying out the main foundations and proofs.

questions.question: What does the image of “steps” help the reader understand about the thirteen mysteries?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that the ideas were meant to be explained one by one in order.

questions.question: What prevented the writer from finishing all thirteen here?
questions.answer: Two strong kinds of obstacles prevented it.

questions.question: What big idea about Allah’s power is highlighted in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s power reaches all things equally, so no created thing is harder for Him than another.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the importance of this idea for Islam?
questions.answer: It describes it as a very important base of Islam and belief.

questions.question: What can this understanding help uncover about the world?
questions.answer: It can help uncover a hidden secret of how all beings are brought into existence.

questions.question: What does the passage say about philosophy’s ability to solve this issue?
questions.answer: It says philosophy cannot handle or solve it.

questions.question: After speaking about this truth, what does the writer do?
questions.answer: He offers great thanks and praise to Allah.

questions.question: What source is presented as giving the solution and proof?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is presented as giving it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the quality of the arguments there?
questions.answer: They are described as decisive and certain.

questions.question: Why does the writer not fully explain everything in this short passage?
questions.answer: Because the full treatment belongs to other sections, and here he only wants to mention the basics briefly.

questions.question: What number of mysteries was planned in the short outline?
questions.answer: Thirteen mysteries.

questions.question: What had the writer managed to write from that plan?
questions.answer: He had managed to write the first two.

questions.question: What caused the work on the rest to stop?
questions.answer: Strong outer and inner obstacles caused it to stop.

questions.question: What is the “mystery” discussed in this passage mostly about?
questions.answer: It is mostly about how Allah creates everything, from the greatest to the smallest, with equal ease.

questions.question: Why is this mystery important for belief in Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: Because it shows a power so complete that only Allah can have it.

questions.question: What does the passage say this explanation opens for the reader?
questions.answer: It opens the deep meaning of the Qur’an and helps reveal a hidden secret in creation.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the power of philosophy compared with this truth?
questions.answer: It suggests philosophy is too weak to reach or solve it.

questions.question: Who is praised with many thanks in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah, the Compassionate Creator.

questions.question: What achievement is credited to the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It is credited with solving, uncovering, and proving this amazing mystery.

questions.question: How sure does the writer say a person can be about those proofs?
questions.answer: A person can be very sure, with strong certainty.

questions.question: What does the writer say he is assigning to certain parts of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: He is leaving the full explanation of this topic to those parts.

questions.question: What does he still want to do in this passage?
questions.answer: He still wants to briefly mention the foundations and proofs and point to thirteen mysteries.

questions.question: What do the thirteen mysteries seem to represent in the writer’s plan?
questions.answer: They seem to represent a step-by-step outline for explaining the subject.

questions.question: Which of the mysteries had already been written?
questions.answer: The first and second.

questions.question: What finally kept the writer from continuing the rest?
questions.answer: Two strong obstacles, one related to the material side and one related to the non-material side.
